text:
sam: heads up — support escalated: multiple customers reporting p95/p99 tail spikes after runtime rollout v2.14 at 2026-03-16T09:10Z. Canary was green but rollout to prod shows p95 ~420ms (was ~180ms). stack: gpu-serving pool A, kernel selector v3.2.

devon: ack. do we have trace links? any common model or sequence lengths?

sam: attaching initial telemetry: most hits for these customers share seq_len ~512 and a sudden bump in kernel selection to slow-path kernels. link: https://grafana.redwood/redirect/rt/abcd1234 (short link)

maya: seeing same in flame graphs — spike aligns with a switch to fused_attention_v1 fallback on some hosts. looks like kernel selection heuristic misclassified.

alex: interesting — canary runs were mostly seq_len 128-256. rollout exposed longer sequences. we should repro with seq=512 load test.

sam: repro script (quick):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROD_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    --data-binary '{"model":"rwd-medium-v1","input":"$(python -c \"print(\'x\' * 512)\")","max_tokens":8}' &
done
wait
```

qa-bot: load test scheduled on staging with identical routing/selector config. ETA 15m.

oncall-bot: alert created: INC-2026-0316-77, paging oncall.

devon: good. two immediate hypotheses: 1) kernel selector update in v3.2 favors stability over perf for long sequences -> slow-path; 2) batching behavior changed (batch sizing limits) causing queuing at tail.

maya: telemetry shows queue depth increases at p99 during those windows. also observed increased inter-request variability (some requests hit slower hosts).

alex: quick mitigation options: revert kernel selector change (v3.1) on pool A, or force routing for model rwd-medium-v1 to older kernel profile; also temporarily increase pool capacity to absorb burst. which is faster?

sam: ops can bump capacity in 5 min. revert needs a config push — prep PR?

devon: pragmatic plan: 1) increase pool A capacity + enable autoscale headroom to damp spikes 2) force route rwd-medium-v1 -> kernel-profile:legacy for traffic for 30m 3) run staged rollback of kernel-selector in canary if tests confirm repro

maya: i'll run the staged repro on canary with forced kernel-profile to confirm perf delta (p95 target < 220ms).

sam: ops — please bump capacity now. tagging @ops.

alex: while ops does that, I'll instrument additional debug logs around kernel selection and add a quick metric: kernel_profile[selected] by model and seq_len bucket.

ops: increased pool A desired count +30% and set autoscale headroom to 40% (done). monitoring for 5m.

qa-bot: staging repro completed: when forcing legacy kernel-profile p95 = 190ms, p99 = 260ms. when using selector v3.2 p95 = 410ms, p99 = 780ms. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/jobs/9876/artifacts/logs

maya: confirms hypothesis. kernel selector heuristic misrouted long sequences to fallback kernel.

devon: recommend fast rollback of selector to v3.1 on pool A and open a follow-up ticket to refine selector thresholds and add seq_len gating. also add a regression test for seq_len=512+ in canary suite.

sam: agreed. I'll file the rollback PR and get approvals. also notifying support with temporary mitigation (increased capacity + routing) and ETA for rollback ~20m.

alex: rolling back selector config on pool A to v3.1 now (config deploy in progress). I'll monitor kernel_profile metric.

oncall-bot: deploy started by alex. change: kernel-selector -> v3.1 on pool A. CI: #4321.

alex: deploy finished. early telemetry: kernel_profile shows legacy = 82% for rwd-medium-v1 seq512 and p95 dropped to ~210ms.

sam: support update: emailed impacted customers with explanation + mitigation steps, promised follow-up post-mortem.

maya: next actions:
- create postmortem draft with timeline, root cause (heuristic change + sequence distribution mismatch), mitigations, and follow-ups
- add regression test in canary that simulates seq_len 512+ traffic to prevent future regressions
- add metric alert: kernel_profile_shift > 20% across seq_len bucket for 10m

devon: and queue a design doc for kernel selector: include seq_len-aware gating, soft fallbacks, and canary traffic weighting by sequence distribution.

sam: thanks everyone. closing the immediate incident. keeping this thread for postmortem comments. :thumbsup:
